reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, equivalent to roughly 275 racks or 2,200 accelerators at typical AI training density, a scale too small to be a binding constraint on large model training.

This facility ranks 22nd among Virginia's 25 data centers with disclosed power capacity and holds 0.7% of the state's total. Virginia itself contains 330 mapped data center locations, but only 25 publish power specifications, meaning the vast majority of the state's infrastructure capacity remains undisclosed. Sterling sits at the regional tier, not hyperscale.

The 128,715 square feet of technical space and absence of any listed certifications indicate a colocation facility built for enterprise and cloud tenants rather than AI-focused operations. Its modest footprint and mid-tier ranking among published Virginia facilities suggest it serves distributed workloads across multiple customers rather than concentrated compute for large-scale model training.

The data does not cover Sterling's actual utilization, power draw, cooling capacity, or any announced expansion. Without broader visibility into Virginia's undisclosed 305 other data center locations, the state's true AI compute footprint remains largely unknown.
